name: Road surface images with seasons — Nashik and Mumbai, Maharashtra (Mendeley Data tj2m7zz4rg, version 2)
publisher: Authors of the Data in Brief article (names not captured); hosted on Mendeley Data
role_summary: PRIORITY real Maharashtra/Indian visual grounding: AI-1 image evaluation at category level (potholes where explicitly labelled), infrastructure-scene coverage and demo realism. Claims limited to what the actual labels support.
version_note: Version 2 of Mendeley Data dataset tj2m7zz4rg (https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/tj2m7zz4rg/2, doi 10.17632/tj2m7zz4rg.2; Data in Brief article PMC8933537). The repository owner confirms this is the exact dataset intended. Reported contents (owner-relayed, not read from the record by this tooling): 8,484 RGB images and 13 videos from Mumbai and Nashik under different road and weather conditions, showing potholes, speed breakers, roadside barriers and paved/unpaved roads. Whether the images carry per-image labels, folder labels or bounding boxes is NOT established: profile the files before any evaluation. A different Kaggle dataset ('Indian Roads Dataset') is explicitly NOT added.

data_access.method: Not hosted on Kaggle by its authors: download the Mendeley files yourself and upload them as a private Kaggle Dataset (so they are read in place from /kaggle/input), keeping the attribution/licence text. This repository never downloads or copies the data.
data_access.video: Videos must be converted to frames outside the repository, keeping the video id in the file/dir name, so holdouts keep whole videos together.

supports.how: Maharashtra road-surface scenes: category-level checks ('damaged road surface' → category roads) and demo realism for the road/surface modality.
caveats: Labels reported at folder/scene level (paved/unpaved/video; damaged, speed breaker, water), not per-pothole boxes: pothole-subcategory evaluation only if the files carry explicit pothole labels.
Speed breakers, paved/unpaved and water-on-road are NOT taxonomy v1 issues (mapped out_of_scope, no new taxonomy category).
Images from the same video/session are near-identical: hold out whole groups.

Label granularity (per-image, folder-level, boxes) unverified: nothing is claimed beyond what profiling shows.
Videos and the images extracted from them (if any) are near-duplicates: whole videos/sequences must be held out together.
